### **1. Connection Diagram for Transformer Efficiency Test (Load Test)**
```text
             +---[ Wattmeter W1 ]---+---[ A1 ]---+--- [ Primary ] ---+
             |                       |                                 |
  Supply ~ --+                       +----[ V1 ]---+                   |
             |                                     |                   |
             +-------------------------------------+-----------------+ |
                                                                     | |
             +------------------------------------ [ Secondary ] ----+
             |                                     |                 |
             |                                  [ V2 ]            [ A2 ] 
             |                                     |                 |
             +---------------------------------[ Load ]--------------+
```

--- 

### **2. Computations**
Given data:
- Transformer Rating = $3\text{ kVA} = 3000\text{ VA}$
- Voltage Rating = $220/110\text{ V}$
- Primary Wattmeter Reading ($P_{in}$) = $550\text{ W}$
- Secondary Wattmeter Reading ($P_{out}$) = $500\text{ W}$

#### **A. Efficiency ($\eta$):**
$$\eta = \frac{\text{Output Power}}{\text{Input Power}} \times 100$$
$$\eta = \frac{500}{550} \times 100 = 90.91\%$$

#### **B. Current Rating of the Transformer:**
- **Primary Current Rating ($I_1$):**
  $$I_1 = \frac{\text{VA Rating}}{V_1} = \frac{3000\text{ VA}}{220\text{ V}} = 13.64\text{ A}$$

- **Secondary Current Rating ($I_2$):**
  $$I_2 = \frac{\text{VA Rating}}{V_2} = \frac{3000\text{ VA}}{110\text{ V}} = 27.27\text{ A}$$
proTip: Efficiency is always output over input. For rating current, always use the nameplate VA rating divided by the respective winding voltage.
